newsitem.title: USA: Midwest labor costs still tame - Chicago Fed.
newsitem.headline: Midwest labor costs still tame - Chicago Fed.

text.p: Labor costs in the Midwest have not accelerated despite extremely strong employment conditions across the region, William Strauss, senior economist at the Chicago Federal Reserve Bank, said Wednesday.
"Our labor markets are exceptionally tight," making the Midwest an important bellwether of employment and wage trends for the nation, Strauss said.
The Fed economist was addressing an economic forum sponsored by the Chicago Board of Trade.

The unemployment rate in the Midwest remains below the national average, running about 1.0 percentage point below the U.S. rate, Strauss said. The U.S. unemployment rate fell to 4.9 percent in April, its lowest level in 24 years.
However, labor costs as measured by the Midwest's employment cost index (ECI) have not risen commensurately as might be expected given the tight local labor market, the Chicago Fed economist said.
"We are beginning to see signs of a pickup in wages," Strauss said, but these have not yet translated into higher production costs.
The lack of upward pressure on costs is illustrated in the ECI, which takes into account productivity in measuring labor expenses, Strauss said.
In the Midwest, ECI rose 2.9 percent in the first quarter year-on-year, in line with the national index, he said.
